Description: Articulate clear compelling vision that attracts talent and customers. Not a mission statement on a wall — a story people want to be part of.
Why_It_Matters: First 10 hires join for the vision not the salary. Investors fund vision. Users evangelize vision.
Do_This: Practice your 'Why' until you can explain it in 30 seconds|Tell stories not features|Repeat vision in every all-hands|Make vision tangible with metrics
Warning_Signs: Cannot explain what you're building in 1 sentence|Team members give different answers about company direction|Vision changes every month
Resources: Start with Why (Simon Sinek)|YC: How to Talk to Users

Description: Most decisions are reversible (Type 2). Move fast on those. Only slow down for irreversible (Type 1) decisions. Bezos framework.
Why_It_Matters: Speed is a competitive advantage for startups. Slow decision-making kills momentum. 70% certainty is enough for Type 2 decisions.
Do_This: Classify: Type 1 (irreversible) or Type 2 (reversible)|70% data = go for Type 2|Set decision deadline (max 48 hrs for Type 2)|Document decisions and reasoning
Warning_Signs: Analysis paralysis on every decision|Treating all decisions as irreversible|No documentation of why decisions were made|Reversing decisions too frequently
Resources: Bezos shareholder letters|Thinking Fast and Slow (Kahneman)

Description: You cannot scale if you do everything. Delegate outcomes not tasks. Trust people to figure out the HOW — you set the WHAT and WHY.
Why_It_Matters: Founders who don't delegate become bottleneck at 5-10 employees. Delegation = multiplying yourself.
Do_This: Start delegating tasks you're 80% good at (not only bad at)|Define outcome + deadline not process|Check in on progress not micromanage|Accept 80% as good enough (they'll do it differently)
Warning_Signs: You're in every meeting|Team asks permission for everything|You redo people's work|You can't take a vacation without chaos
Resources: High Output Management (Andy Grove)|The Manager's Path (Camille Fournier)

Description: Burnout is the #1 silent killer of startups. Not lack of funding. Work-rest cycles are not a luxury — they're a strategic advantage.
Why_It_Matters: Burned out founders make bad decisions: wrong hires, wrong pivots, wrong investments. Your decision quality IS the company quality.
Do_This: Set hard stopping time (not flexible)|Exercise 3x/week minimum|Weekly no-work day (non-negotiable)|Peer group or coach for venting|Recognize early signs: cynicism, exhaustion, detachment
Warning_Signs: Working 7 days/week consistently|Skipping exercise for months|No social life outside work|Irritable with team|Making impulsive decisions
Resources: Burn Rate (Andy Dunn)|The Hard Thing About Hard Things (Ben Horowitz)|OSMI.org

Description: Technical founders often underinvest in EQ. But managing people requires understanding emotions — yours and theirs. EQ \u003e IQ for leadership.
Why_It_Matters: High-EQ founders have lower turnover, better team morale, and navigate conflict constructively. Investors notice EQ in meetings.
Do_This: Practice active listening (repeat back what you heard)|Name your emotions before reacting|Ask 'what do you think?' before sharing your opinion|Regular self-reflection (journaling)|Seek honest feedback on your blind spots
Warning_Signs: Reacting emotionally in meetings|Never admitting mistakes|Dismissing team emotions as 'drama'|Avoiding difficult conversations

Description: Conflict is inevitable and healthy. Avoidance makes it worse. Learn to address issues directly, privately, and constructively.
Why_It_Matters: Unresolved conflict destroys teams faster than any external threat. Most co-founder breakups are from avoided conversations.
Do_This: Address within 48 hours (never let it fester)|Private conversation (never public)|Use 'I observed X' not 'You always Y'|Seek to understand before being understood|Document agreements
Warning_Signs: Avoiding conflict hoping it resolves|Public criticism|Taking sides without hearing both|No follow-up after resolution

Description: Startups are a series of near-death experiences. Resilience isn't about not failing — it's reframing failure as data and continuing.
Why_It_Matters: Every successful founder has a 'almost quit' story. The ones who succeed reframe hardship. Active resilience = processing failure constructively.
Do_This: Reframe setbacks as experiments (data not failure)|Build support network (other founders)|Celebrate small wins weekly|Keep a 'wins journal'|Physical health = mental resilience
Warning_Signs: Comparing to others' highlight reels|Isolating when things go wrong|Toxic positivity (denying problems exist)|No recovery time after major setbacks

Description: Most founders feel like frauds at some point. It's universal. The difference: successful founders act despite the doubt, not without it.
Why_It_Matters: Imposter syndrome peaks at fundraising, first hires, and public launches. Unmanaged, it leads to over-preparation, under-delegation, and burnout.
Do_This: Talk to other founders (they feel it too)|Track objective achievements|Separate 'feeling unqualified' from 'being unqualified'|Accept that discomfort means growth|Seek mentors who normalize the struggle
Warning_Signs: Not applying because you feel unready|Over-preparing to compensate|Dismissing your own achievements|Comparing your beginning to others' middle
Resources: Code Review Anxiety Workbook|OSMI resources|Founder communities (Indie Hackers)

Description: Are YOU the right person to solve THIS problem? Founder-market fit = unfair advantage. You've lived the problem, know the domain, have unique insight.
Why_It_Matters: Investors evaluate founder-market fit. Users trust founders who've experienced the problem. Domain expertise reduces time to PMF by 2-3x.
Do_This: Customer zero check: did you experience this problem?|Domain expertise: can you explain the landscape without slides?|Network advantage: do you know the first 10 customers?|Passion endurance: will you care about this in 5 years?
Warning_Signs: Building in a domain you don't understand|No personal connection to the problem|Chasing trends instead of genuine interest|Can't name 10 people who have this problem
Resources: The Mom Test (Rob Fitzpatrick)|YC How to Evaluate Startup Ideas

Description: Investor relationship management: regular updates, transparent bad news, ask for specific help. Good investor updates = strong relationship.
Why_It_Matters: Good investor relationships unlock intro networks, follow-on funding, and strategic advice. Bad relationships = stress and interference.
Do_This: Monthly investor update (5 min read)|Include: wins, losses, asks, KPIs|Share bad news early (before it's crisis)|Ask for specific help (intros, advice, hiring)|Build relationship before you need money
Warning_Signs: Hiding bad news|Only reaching out when you need something|Overly long updates|Not asking for help|Surprising investors with bad news at board meetings
